vocabulary.definition: a verb that is made up of a main verb together with an adverb or a preposition or both, and the meaning of the phrasal verb is different from the meanings of its individual parts
vocabulary.example: To get on with someone is a useful phrasal verb, meaning to like someone and enjoy a friendly relationship with them.

vocabulary.definition: a good feeling between two people based on understanding and communication
vocabulary.example: Building rapport with 'terrorists' or violent criminals isn't easy.

vocabulary.definition: a difficult situation that requires careful consideration of what to do
vocabulary.example: Emily describes rapport building as like walking a tightrope.

vocabulary.definition: basing your actions on facts rather than personal feelings
vocabulary.example: Emily tries to remain objective when building rapport with criminal suspects.

vocabulary.definition: saying the opposite of what you really mean, in order to hurt someone's feelings or criticize them in a humorous way
vocabulary.example: T-Rex types can be sarcastic, saying things that they don't really mean.

vocabulary.definition: showing that you understand and care about someone's problems
vocabulary.example: Emily doesn't sympathize with the actions of violent criminals but tries to remain objective.
